recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Only revisit if a new work-group decision specifically changes CapabilityStatement.software.releaseDate semantics; FHIR-2949 itself is already reconciled.
issue_request: FHIR-2949 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. The summary asked whether Conformance.software.releaseDate should be date instead of dateTime, while the accepted resolution said software can be released multiple times per day and requested descriptive wording for date and optional time of publication.
initial_application: The Jira comment records application in SVN revision 2993. The corresponding git-svn commit f00a9c5fe9ab6a16ad9ecdd729436b09e7e84864 changed Conformance.date from publication date wording to publication date/time wording and left the datatype as dateTime; later renames and source refactors carried that into CapabilityStatement.date.
additional_context: CapabilityStatement is active build-scope source in fhir.ini and normative from 4.0.0. The current CapabilityStatement.date element is dateTime and still says date and optionally time, with later FHIR-37858 history explaining the shift from publication date to last significant change. CapabilityStatement.software.releaseDate also remains dateTime, and the primitive dateTime definition permits date-only, date-time, or partial-date precision.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. Changing software.releaseDate to date-only would conflict with the accepted rationale allowing same-day releases, and adding duplicate optional-time prose is unnecessary because the datatype and the active successor element already convey the intended rule.

related_jiras.note: Later applied change clarified CanonicalResource.date-style wording from publication date to last significant change, explaining current CapabilityStatement.date prose.
